risks: Minimal: review of existing records by the ambulance service's own audit team. The risk is blame of individual crews, avoided by reporting at service level.
consent: Not sought: clinical audit of routine records by the service's own team under its governance approval.
data: Records stay within the ambulance service; the audit spreadsheet holds incident numbers, not names; no hospital data are accessed.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: rural residence, age over 65 and sex may affect whether the drug is given. Results are reported by age band, sex and transport time band, and remote areas are shown separately.
effectiveness: Useful if it shows where the pathway fails so that training or crew support can be targeted.
efficiency: Uses existing records and governance time.
costs: Audit team time within existing roles.
grants: None needed; a linked outcome analysis might seek regional funding later.
partnerships: Ambulance service audit team, paramedic educators, the three hospitals' trauma leads, and a patient representative from the network's trauma survivors group.
rebPath: Approved as clinical audit by the ambulance service's audit committee (CA-EMS-2026-22). Any linked outcome analysis would need a renewed data-sharing agreement and research ethics review of secondary use before it starts.
limitations: No outcomes; eligibility and injury time depend on record quality.
summary: Approved clinical audit of ambulance records; outcome work waits for the data-sharing agreement and ethics review.
